title_en: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures
title_fa: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures
excerpt_en: Sources say more cuts could follow as the company looks to improve its finances.
excerpt_fa: Sources say more cuts could follow as the company looks to improve its finances.
content_en:
Automattic, the parent company to WordPress.com, WooCommerce, Tumblr, and others, has begun layoffs, and insiders tell us they are bracing for more cuts to come.
Over at least the past week, the cuts have impacted its communications team, social team, WordPress.com, and its VIP enterprise business.
The departures represent more turmoil at Automattic, whose team is still reeling from the board’s failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg in September, resulting in a complete board turnover and other exec departures, including its CFO, interim CFO, and chief legal officer.
Automattic’s director of communications, Megan Fox, posted about her departure last week on LinkedIn, saying the move was an “unexpected end” and that her role had been “eliminated.”
Meanwhile, after TechCrunch reported that Automattic’s interim CFO Jeremy Klaperman left earlier this month, only weeks after the board shake-up, Mullenweg posted on X suggesting Klaperman may have been “offended” by the company’s decision to seek external candidates to fill the role. (Internally, however, Mullenweg had asked Klaperman to reconsider leaving, we had heard.)
At one point, Mullenweg also shared personal information about one of the recently departed execs in the company’s internal Slack, according to screenshots viewed by TechCrunch. The post was related to a health matter impacting the person’s spouse and claimed that the company was not providing this person with much-needed COBRA insurance. Mullenweg said the exec was threatening to sue over this. Mullenweg also shared that his own fiancée had been impacted by the same health condition. Some employees told us they were shocked that the CEO would share something so private and personal in such a forum.
Throughout this month, TechCrunch has heard from different sources that members of Automattic’s team have also been let go, including those in marketing and product at WordPress.com.
Reached for comment about the layoffs last week, Mullenweg said the terminations were not above its normal numbers. Asked on Wednesday about the growing total, Mullenweg said that today he was “mostly focused on PHP.” (He posted on X about the PHP security issue hitting the internet, which is taking priority.)
The company’s About page lists the total number of staff at 1,397, but insiders tell us that the plan is likely to spread out the layoffs over the months ahead, in the hopes of improving Automattic’s Q4 revenue figures ahead of a debt renegotiation that’s coming up in June.
In a statement shared with TechCrunch, Automattic spokesperson Chenda Ngak said, “We’re staggering our organizational changes to be more generous with severance and allow more time with each Automattician.”
Updated after publication with Automattic’s statement.

title_en: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
title_fa: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
excerpt_en: Bose announced today it has acquired Skullcandy. Although the two companies are competitors in the consumer audio space, Skullcandy recently partnered with its new owner to bring several of Bose's audio technologies - including its head-tracking spatial audio and excellent...
excerpt_fa: Bose announced today it has acquired Skullcandy. Although the two companies are competitors in the consumer audio space, Skullcandy recently partnered with its new owner to bring several of Bose's audio technologies - including its head-tracking spatial audio and excellent...
content_en:
Bose announced today it has acquired Skullcandy. Although the two companies are competitors in the consumer audio space, Skullcandy recently partnered with its new owner to bring several of Bose’s audio technologies — including its head-tracking spatial audio and excellent active noise cancellation (ANC) — to products like the Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and Method 360 ANC earbuds.
Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
Bose will leverage Skullcandy’s designs and branding to help the company reach new demographics.
Bose will leverage Skullcandy’s designs and branding to help the company reach new demographics.
Specific details about the deal weren’t shared, but according to a news release, Bose plans to keep Skullcandy a separate brand that will become part of its premium consumer audio business. Skullcandy will remain based in Park City, Utah, where it was founded. The acquisition will help Bose expand the reach of its audio technologies, including its industry-leading noise cancellation, to a wider audience.
“For more than 60 years, Bose has been committed to delivering incredible audio experiences however and wherever people choose to listen. As we work to reach even more people, we’re expanding how we do that, not only through Bose products, but through technology partnerships and a growing portfolio of brands,” Bose CEO Lila Snyder says.
Founded in 2003, Skullcandy hasn’t been around for as long as Bose has, but the company’s distinct product designs and branding that includes “longstanding relationships” with board sports athletes will “present new ways for Bose to meaningfully connect with consumers where it has less presence today,” according to today’s release. Bose’s products are a staple among people who regularly fly and travel for work, but Skullcandy will help the company’s products appeal to consumers who don’t necessarily prioritize the effectiveness of ANC on their headphones.
In 2024, Bose acquired the high-end audio brand McIntosh and its subsidiary Sonus faber, and this year it acquired StreamUnlimited Engineering and FMOD-maker Firelight Technologies. Bose also announced last June it had created an in-house content studio called Bose Studios, as well as its own record label, Bose Records.

title_en: Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
title_fa: Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
excerpt_en: Checking out of your next Airbnb might be less of a hassle now that the company is banning hosts from including time-consuming chores in their house rules. Airbnb's updated house rules policy, which starts with reservations booked on or after November 20th, says hosts can't ask...
excerpt_fa: Checking out of your next Airbnb might be less of a hassle now that the company is banning hosts from including time-consuming chores in their house rules. Airbnb's updated house rules policy, which starts with reservations booked on or after November 20th, says hosts can't ask...
content_en:
Checking out of your next Airbnb might be less of a hassle now that the company is banning hosts from including time-consuming chores in their house rules. Airbnb’s updated house rules policy, which starts with reservations booked on or after November 20th, says hosts can’t ask guests to “complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner.” According to Airbnb, that includes:
Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
Airbnb’s new rules limit hosts to ‘reasonable’ requests like putting dirty dishes in the sink.
Airbnb’s new rules limit hosts to ‘reasonable’ requests like putting dirty dishes in the sink.
- Dishes: Guests shouldn’t be asked to wash and put away dishes, but you can ask them to put used dishes in the sink.
- Laundry: Guests shouldn’t be asked to remove sheets from the bed or start a load of laundry, but you can ask them to gather used towels.
- Trash: Guests shouldn’t be asked to take garbage off-site, but you can ask them to separate their trash and recycling into designated indoor bins.
- Utilities: Guests shouldn’t be asked to avoid using a listed amenity like air conditioning, but you can ask them to turn it off when they leave.
Airbnb is displaying hosts’ requests more prominently now in a new “rules and requests” section on listings. You might see an “includes cleaning requests” warning if a host leaves chore requests in their listing after the new policy goes into effect. Hosts aren’t allowed to sneak in extra rules in messages to guests or on signs around their property, either.
Some hosts pushed back on the house rules restrictions on Airbnb’s forums, saying they pose health risks and arguing that guests can simply choose not to stay at listings with overly-strict rules. Airbnb says there can be exceptions to the limits on checkout chores, like asking guests to “dispose of trash in an animal-proof container in bear country.”

title_en: Xbox is previewing paid cloud gaming for players without Game Pass
title_fa: Xbox is previewing paid cloud gaming for players without Game Pass
excerpt_en: Here come new rate limits.
excerpt_fa: Here come new rate limits.
content_en:
Xbox is previewing paid cloud gaming for players without Game Pass
Subscribers will start seeing limits on their free streaming next month.
Xbox has been overhauling several of its gaming offerings in recent months as the company pivots under its new leadership. One of the upcoming changes is to cloud gaming, with plans to apply time limits of five to 15 hours for how long Game Pass subscribers can stream each month. In advance of those changes in November, Xbox is rolling out early previews of cloud playtime for people in its Xbox Insider program who don't have a Game Pass subscription. Xbox Insider lets players try out features early and provide feedback ahead of their official launch.
During this phase, players can purchase cloud gaming access in blocks of 10 hours for $4, 25 hours for $8 or 50 hours for $12. Those rates are being called the "introductory launch prices," so it's possible the final costs could still change next month when Game Pass subscribers will also have to pay to go beyond the new time limits.
Cloud playtime purchases unlock "an ad-free cloud gaming experience, including shorter wait times, high-quality streaming, and playtime that remains available until it's used." People in the Insiders program have also been able to try ad-supported cloud streaming for free since the summer.

title_en: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
title_fa: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
excerpt_en: To compete with Tesla, Rivian, and a host of Chinese automakers, GM’s fourth-gen EV platform will roll out a new central computer and electrical architecture that will debut in 2028 in the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
excerpt_fa: To compete with Tesla, Rivian, and a host of Chinese automakers, GM’s fourth-gen EV platform will roll out a new central computer and electrical architecture that will debut in 2028 in the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
content_en:
When GM announced its new fourth-generation EV platform on Wednesday, what the automaker didn’t share was almost as notable as what it did.
The new EV platform, part of a series of technology-focused announcements made during its annual GM Forward event in New York, didn’t talk about suspension geometries, dash-to-axle ratios, and torsional rigidity, all nerdy automotive terms that translate to how people will experience a car. Is it supple or sporty? Does it have a refined stance? When it hits a pothole, does it feel like a bank vault or a paper plate?
Instead, GM’s announcement centered on novel battery chemistries, revamped electric motors, and an entirely new central computing platform and electrical architecture that will connect every system in the car, including acceleration and power, steering, braking, and active safety features as well as software. Lots and lots of software.
“We think vehicles can become a more capable and helpful part of everyday life if we make them spaces that understand context, reduce friction, and give people back moments that would otherwise be consumed by the demands of the road,” Sterling Anderson, executive vice president, global product, and chief product officer at GM, told TechCrunch in a recent interview.
That sure doesn’t sound like a traditional automaker’s pitch. Then again, since the arrival of Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese automakers, the industry hasn’t been the same. Ride and handling still matter, but they’re table stakes. What sets vehicles apart today is largely defined by software.
Anderson has talked about this future GM before. Last year, the company announced plans to overhaul the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant.
This year, GM is providing more details and dates. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over.
The software race includes hardware
European and U.S. automakers have spent years chasing the prospect of software-defined vehicles but have often fallen short. Volkswagen Group had so much trouble with its own in-house effort, including its troubled Cariad unit, that it struck a $5.8 billion joint venture deal with relative newcomer Rivian.
GM has been on its own capitally intensive software adventure. The company has bet heavily on software in recent years. It ditched the popular smartphone projection technology Apple CarPlay for nearly all of its EVs, and instead turned to a Google-based infotainment system, which is actually quite capable even if it doesn’t yet live up to the standards set by Tesla and Rivian.
It’s poured billions into software and autonomous vehicle technology development too. GM’s capitalized software amortization expense in 2025 was $866 million, which gives a sense of how much it is spending even as it spreads out the cost over years.
Like many legacy automakers, GM has come to the conclusion that the old approach to electronics, which scattered computer chips throughout the vehicle, was holding it back.
For fourth-generation EVs, GM will centralize much of those functions on a central compute unit (CCU) that’s 40x more powerful than its existing systems. Eliminating smaller chips on the edges will help trim wiring by 30%, saving weight and simplifying assembly.
GM notes that this new CCU will work on fossil fuel models, too, though it will debut in the Cadillac Escalade IQ, a vehicle that is shaping up to be the automaker’s technological flagship.
The CCU will handle the usual propulsion and chassis controls, as well as perception and active safety. That should help pave the way for more advanced autonomy features, which GM also announced on Wednesday.
Such a move was perhaps inevitable. Pressure on automakers has been building on all sides.
Domestically, Tesla has been pushing the boundaries of autonomy, in part because it developed a true software-defined vehicle.
Automakers like GM are also feeling pressure from Chinese manufacturers, which have shortened development cycles to two to three years, down from the usual four to five years.
GM intends to match that cadence. Alongside announcements about battery chemistries and autonomy, GM outlined how enterprise AI tools have sped up vehicle development across every sector as it pushes to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half.
GM gave a brief glimpse of its revamped development strategy. One example: Engineers went through 300,000 virtual designs of a new lithium-manganese-rich battery pack before they assembled the first physical prototype. That helped the concept move to an approved program in one month.
Such speed will help GM save costs as it races to preserve profitability amid a historic upheaval in the automotive industry. But will it be enough to catapult it back into the leadership position it once enjoyed?
The rise of Chinese automakers won’t make it easy. Their factories are capable of producing far more than Chinese consumers can absorb, and coupled with government subsidies and cheaper labor, these vehicles have flooded markets from Europe to South America with inexpensive vehicles.
Chinese automakers’ cost advantage is so steep that, without trade barriers, “they will pretty much demolish most other companies in the world,” Elon Musk said in a 2024 earnings call. In response, he has been trying to pivot Tesla from an automotive company to an AI and robotics company.
GM’s move into autonomy signals a similar shift. But to deliver true autonomy, GM realized it didn’t have the platform it needed. With a new architecture, it should have a fighting chance.

The new EV platform, part of a series of technology-focused announcements made during its annual GM Forward event in New York, didn’t talk about suspension geometries, dash-to-axle ratios, and torsional rigidity, all nerdy automotive terms that translate to how people will experience a car. Is it supple or sporty? Does it have a refined stance? When it hits a pothole, does it feel like a bank vault or a paper plate?
Instead, GM’s announcement centered on novel battery chemistries, revamped electric motors, and an entirely new central computing platform and electrical architecture that will connect every system in the car, including acceleration and power, steering, braking, and active safety features as well as software. Lots and lots of software.
“We think vehicles can become a more capable and helpful part of everyday life if we make them spaces that understand context, reduce friction, and give people back moments that would otherwise be consumed by the demands of the road,” Sterling Anderson, executive vice president, global product, and chief product officer at GM, told TechCrunch in a recent interview.
That sure doesn’t sound like a traditional automaker’s pitch. Then again, since the arrival of Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese automakers, the industry hasn’t been the same. Ride and handling still matter, but they’re table stakes. What sets vehicles apart today is largely defined by software.
Anderson has talked about this future GM before. Last year, the company announced plans to overhaul the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant.
This year, GM is providing more details and dates. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over.
The software race includes hardware
European and U.S. automakers have spent years chasing the prospect of software-defined vehicles but have often fallen short. Volkswagen Group had so much trouble with its own in-house effort, including its troubled Cariad unit, that it struck a $5.8 billion joint venture deal with relative newcomer Rivian.
GM has been on its own capitally intensive software adventure. The company has bet heavily on software in recent years. It ditched the popular smartphone projection technology Apple CarPlay for nearly all of its EVs, and instead turned to a Google-based infotainment system, which is actually quite capable even if it doesn’t yet live up to the standards set by Tesla and Rivian.
It’s poured billions into software and autonomous vehicle technology development too. GM’s capitalized software amortization expense in 2025 was $866 million, which gives a sense of how much it is spending even as it spreads out the cost over years.
Like many legacy automakers, GM has come to the conclusion that the old approach to electronics, which scattered computer chips throughout the vehicle, was holding it back.
For fourth-generation EVs, GM will centralize much of those functions on a central compute unit (CCU) that’s 40x more powerful than its existing systems. Eliminating smaller chips on the edges will help trim wiring by 30%, saving weight and simplifying assembly.
GM notes that this new CCU will work on fossil fuel models, too, though it will debut in the Cadillac Escalade IQ, a vehicle that is shaping up to be the automaker’s technological flagship.
The CCU will handle the usual propulsion and chassis controls, as well as perception and active safety. That should help pave the way for more advanced autonomy features, which GM also announced on Wednesday.
Such a move was perhaps inevitable. Pressure on automakers has been building on all sides.
Domestically, Tesla has been pushing the boundaries of autonomy, in part because it developed a true software-defined vehicle.
Automakers like GM are also feeling pressure from Chinese manufacturers, which have shortened development cycles to two to three years, down from the usual four to five years.
GM intends to match that cadence. Alongside announcements about battery chemistries and autonomy, GM outlined how enterprise AI tools have sped up vehicle development across every sector as it pushes to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half.
GM gave a brief glimpse of its revamped development strategy. One example: Engineers went through 300,000 virtual designs of a new lithium-manganese-rich battery pack before they assembled the first physical prototype. That helped the concept move to an approved program in one month.
Such speed will help GM save costs as it races to preserve profitability amid a historic upheaval in the automotive industry. But will it be enough to catapult it back into the leadership position it once enjoyed?
The rise of Chinese automakers won’t make it easy. Their factories are capable of producing far more than Chinese consumers can absorb, and coupled with government subsidies and cheaper labor, these vehicles have flooded markets from Europe to South America with inexpensive vehicles.
Chinese automakers’ cost advantage is so steep that, without trade barriers, “they will pretty much demolish most other companies in the world,” Elon Musk said in a 2024 earnings call. In response, he has been trying to pivot Tesla from an automotive company to an AI and robotics company.
GM’s move into autonomy signals a similar shift. But to deliver true autonomy, GM realized it didn’t have the platform it needed. With a new architecture, it should have a fighting chance.

title_en: Meta ordered to pay $25B in case related to Cambridge Analytica scandal
title_fa: Meta ordered to pay $25B in case related to Cambridge Analytica scandal
excerpt_en: The payout is related to a recent trial involving the social media giant that revolved around its data privacy practices.
excerpt_fa: The payout is related to a recent trial involving the social media giant that revolved around its data privacy practices.
content_en:
The tale of the Cambridge Analytica data scandal is long — and it keeps costing Meta gargantuan sums of money.
On Wednesday, a judge ordered the social media giant to initiate its biggest payout yet: $25 billion to the state of New Mexico for the tech giant’s role in deceiving resident users over its data privacy practices, The New York Times reports.
The huge sum follows a two-week trial in which a New Mexico jury deliberated over the company’s alleged wrongdoing. The jury found that the company behind Facebook and Instagram had committed 43 million violations of the state’s consumer protection laws, each of which carried a $5,000 penalty, the outlet notes.
Part of the case revolved around the company’s handling of a third-party app linked to the Cambridge Analytica data breach, The Wall Street Journal reports. Other parts involved its data privacy policies and its efforts to mitigate misinformation on its platform.
Cambridge Analytica was an outgrowth of a British defense contractor, SLC Group, that specialized in influence operations and other political work. The company notably worked with the Trump campaign during the 2016 presidential election. It was also involved in a number of controversial initiatives.
“We may have paid for the construction of schools for the next 100 years,” New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez told journalists at a press conference, commenting on the case’s resolution.
Meta said that it will appeal the decision.
“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” said C.J. Mahoney, Meta’s chief legal officer, in a statement shared with TechCrunch via email. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online. We are confident we will prevail on appeal. In the meantime, Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge,” he added.

title_en: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
title_fa: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
excerpt_en: As Amazon blocks AI agents from shopping on its site, Walmart is taking the opposite approach, introducing new technology that lets AI agents make purchases on customers' behalf, with controls over spending and transaction approvals.
excerpt_fa: As Amazon blocks AI agents from shopping on its site, Walmart is taking the opposite approach, introducing new technology that lets AI agents make purchases on customers' behalf, with controls over spending and transaction approvals.
content_en:
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.
The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely. Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.
Now it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart president and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.
It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.
What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.
The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.
With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.
The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending.
The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.
Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.
Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

title_en: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day
title_fa: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day
excerpt_en: From AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities to flaws in Node.js and popular AI tool LiteLLM, cybersecurity teams have plenty to worry about this week.
excerpt_fa: From AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities to flaws in Node.js and popular AI tool LiteLLM, cybersecurity teams have plenty to worry about this week.
content_en:
The internet is having a bad day, from a cybersecurity perspective. Government websites around the world went offline, Reuters reported, after AI discovered critical security vulnerabilities that impacted the programming language PHP. The issues were severe enough that the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) advised organizations using PHP on their systems to either immediately update or take their systems offline until they could.
But the PHP update wasn’t the only headache cybersecurity folks were facing on Wednesday. Node.js, the open source JavaScript runtime environment, also dropped a security surprise of its own when it shared that four high-severity vulnerabilities were just patched in its latest release. One allowed remote code execution, and two others would have permitted a TLS validation bypass, potentially allowing attackers to bypass checks intended to verify a server’s identity.
In addition, LiteLLM, a popular open source proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code, the company shared in a post on X on Wednesday afternoon. The malicious artifacts were published to PyPI (Python Package Index), Docker Hub, and GHCR (GitHub Container Registry), the post noted.
The malicious code was said to include an information stealer that targeted cloud credentials, passwords, and AI service credentials, in addition to a remote access trojan that could allow hackers to execute commands on compromised systems.
LiteLLM said it has now removed the malicious releases and images and advised anyone who installed them to follow the remediation guidance it provided.
And wait, there’s more! An Indian certificate authority, eMudhra, had its private keys compromised, potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. Security pros have called this a massive cleanup job and one that’s “bigger than Heartbleed.” (The latter is a reference to the critical security vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptographic software library.)
These issues come on the heels of other security breaches and hacks, including the breach of the cloud-native database-as-a-service, TiDB Cloud, which the company announced on Monday. Other hackers have been exploiting four patched Plex Media Server flaws, collectively called Plex2Shell. And last week, cybersecurity company BeyondTrust warned customers to patch a critical zero-day in its Remote Support product, which had been exploited since August.
Though the issues were unrelated to each other, their back-to-back arrival highlights the challenges cybersecurity teams now face. This is particularly important as AI could make it easier for attackers to exploit vulnerabilities once discovered.

title_en: Legal AI startup Legora raises $550M Series E at $8.8B valuation
title_fa: Legal AI startup Legora raises $550M Series E at $8.8B valuation
excerpt_en: Legal AI startup Legora announced Wednesday that it raised a $550 million Series E round, valuing it at $8.8 billion.
excerpt_fa: Legal AI startup Legora announced Wednesday that it raised a $550 million Series E round, valuing it at $8.8 billion.
content_en:
Legal AI startup Legora announced Wednesday that it raised a $550 million Series E round, valuing it at $8.8 billion.
The company helps automate and assist with workflow tasks for legal professionals, as the industry moves beyond AI assistants to AI services that help them get work done.
The news comes just a month after Harvey, Legora’s biggest competitor, announced a $550 million raise at a $15.5 billion valuation; back in March, Harvey also said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) was more than $ 200 million.
Legora’s Series E follows the company’s April announcement of a $50 million extension of a $550 million Series D round, which valued the company at $5.6 billion. At the time, the company said its ARR had reached $100 million. That number now stands at over $200 million, the company shared on Wednesday.
Investors in the latest financing include Atreides Management, which led the round, as well as Baron Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Menlo, and other top names. The company plans to use the fresh capital to further expand across North America.

title_en: EA is shutting down BioWare and cutting around 400 jobs
title_fa: EA is shutting down BioWare and cutting around 400 jobs
excerpt_en: Skate studio Full Circle will be be reduced to "a more focused, smaller team," while a Sims project has been paused.
excerpt_fa: Skate studio Full Circle will be be reduced to "a more focused, smaller team," while a Sims project has been paused.
content_en:
EA is shutting down BioWare and cutting around 400 jobs
Skate studio Full Circle will be be reduced too.
Changes were always going to be in store for Electronic Arts after the company went private and its new owners saddled it with $20 billion of debt. EA announced some alterations to the business on Wednesday, which include layoffs and the shut down of Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare.
The studio had struggled in recent years after Anthem (which shut down earlier this year) and Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet sales expectations. EA, which bought BioWare in 2007, said a small team was in the early stages of work on the next Mass Effect game. However, it decided to cancel that project and close BioWare entirely, along with its office in Edmonton, Alberta.
"BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," a memo from EA co-presidents Cam Weber and David Tinson reads.
— BioWare (@bioware) October 21, 2026
Overall, EA is laying off around three percent of its workforce, according to Variety — approximately 400 people. EA said it will help affected workers "in exploring other opportunities" within the company.
Among the studios that are losing workers is Skate developer Full Circle. The memo states the game, which has been in early access since September last year, has had "a lot of success" with bringing in players. Still, EA is "making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business."
At The Sims developer Maxis, EA is pausing development of what it calls "Project Lotus" in order to funnel more resources into another initiative dubbed Project Evergreen.
EA also touched on what's ahead for other studios. Along with working on Battlefield projects and Apex Legends (which has more multiplayer modes on the way), Respawn and Dice are collaborating on a new shooter. According to Variety's sources, that will be Star Wars: Battlefront 3. Rumors suggested this week that multiple studios were in the running to make that game, including Bungie, but it seems the series is staying within EA. Dice was the developer of the last two Star Wars: Battlefront titles.
Elsewhere, after Marvel's Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi game, EA says it will "concentrate our efforts on fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects" in the action adventure space. As for EA Sports, that division is bringing back the Fight Night series while the American football team is working on a "brand-new, social-first open-world experience." EA plans to announce more details about those projects in the next few months.

title_en: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover
title_fa: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover
excerpt_en: It's one of the biggest overhauls ever to the 30-year-old connected car product.
excerpt_fa: It's one of the biggest overhauls ever to the 30-year-old connected car product.
content_en:
General Motors is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar as part of a broader makeover of the subscription-based connected car service that the U.S. automaker launched 30 years ago.
The OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV in the coming months, with more GM vehicles to follow, the company said Wednesday at its GM Forward event in New York, where it made a series of other technology announcements covering software, automated driving, EVs, and its electrical architecture. The company said it will launch a new OnStar mobile app in 2027 that will complement and sync up with its in-car software.
The new OnStar mobile app will replace the current OnStar Guardian app that launched in 2020 as well as vehicle brand apps for Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC.
This tech-centric reboot is unlike other attempts to modernize OnStar, and it notably puts agentic AI at the center. The company has updated the safety and roadside assistance service numerous times in its history, especially in the past five years as it tried to stay apace of emerging and tech-forward competitors like Tesla.
In 2021, the company expanded its OnStar Guardian app, which offered crash detection, emergency assistance, and location sharing to anyone with a compatible phone, even if they didn’t own a GM vehicle. A year later, GM started using Google Cloud’s conversational AI Dialogflow to recognize specific spoken requests and expanded in 2023 to give drivers responses to common queries like routing and navigation assistance — all part of GM’s plan to build a $25 billion subscription business by 2030.
GM continued to focus on generative AI but relied on Google to provide the experience. The company said last year that Google Gemini would roll out in vehicles in 2026.
The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house effort and one aimed at giving the driver and passengers an interactive and custom experience — and become even more embedded in their daily lives.
“OnStar is now transitioning to be a connected intelligence platform, not just the call center that it’s historically been known as, but a mechanism for interpreting, understanding, and providing predictive, proactive support to its owners,” GM’s VP of global product and chief product officer Sterling Anderson told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the GM Forward event.
For instance, cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users can set up the connected cameras to turn on automatically if the vehicle senses an impending event — such as an aggressive horn honk — then capture the event and upload it to the OnStar app. Users will be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.
The launch coincides with efforts throughout the auto industry to stay apace of Chinese automakers with technology that is central to the vehicle — and no longer a slapped-on gimmick or feature. But that has required GM to change its approach to software development, adopt AI tools, and even design a new electrical and centralized compute vehicle architecture.
The announcement also comes after GM has been criticized and even fined for sharing data with third parties. Earlier this year, the Federal Trade Commission finalized an order that bans General Motors and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data with consumer reporting agencies. The finalized order also requires the automaker to be more transparent with its consumers and obtain their explicit consent on certain data collection.
GM said Wednesday that customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings.
A GM spokesperson later stated that third-party sharing is “feature-specific and consent-based, with information shared only as needed to provide requested functionality.” Customers can manage permissions and withdraw consent; however, those who choose not to share certain data may have limited access to related features, while other OnStar services would continue, according to GM.
This article was updated to include comments from a GM spokesperson.
content_fa:
General Motors is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar as part of a broader makeover of the subscription-based connected car service that the U.S. automaker launched 30 years ago.
The OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV in the coming months, with more GM vehicles to follow, the company said Wednesday at its GM Forward event in New York, where it made a series of other technology announcements covering software, automated driving, EVs, and its electrical architecture. The company said it will launch a new OnStar mobile app in 2027 that will complement and sync up with its in-car software.
The new OnStar mobile app will replace the current OnStar Guardian app that launched in 2020 as well as vehicle brand apps for Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC.
This tech-centric reboot is unlike other attempts to modernize OnStar, and it notably puts agentic AI at the center. The company has updated the safety and roadside assistance service numerous times in its history, especially in the past five years as it tried to stay apace of emerging and tech-forward competitors like Tesla.
In 2021, the company expanded its OnStar Guardian app, which offered crash detection, emergency assistance, and location sharing to anyone with a compatible phone, even if they didn’t own a GM vehicle. A year later, GM started using Google Cloud’s conversational AI Dialogflow to recognize specific spoken requests and expanded in 2023 to give drivers responses to common queries like routing and navigation assistance — all part of GM’s plan to build a $25 billion subscription business by 2030.
GM continued to focus on generative AI but relied on Google to provide the experience. The company said last year that Google Gemini would roll out in vehicles in 2026.
The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house effort and one aimed at giving the driver and passengers an interactive and custom experience — and become even more embedded in their daily lives.
“OnStar is now transitioning to be a connected intelligence platform, not just the call center that it’s historically been known as, but a mechanism for interpreting, understanding, and providing predictive, proactive support to its owners,” GM’s VP of global product and chief product officer Sterling Anderson told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the GM Forward event.
For instance, cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users can set up the connected cameras to turn on automatically if the vehicle senses an impending event — such as an aggressive horn honk — then capture the event and upload it to the OnStar app. Users will be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.
The launch coincides with efforts throughout the auto industry to stay apace of Chinese automakers with technology that is central to the vehicle — and no longer a slapped-on gimmick or feature. But that has required GM to change its approach to software development, adopt AI tools, and even design a new electrical and centralized compute vehicle architecture.
The announcement also comes after GM has been criticized and even fined for sharing data with third parties. Earlier this year, the Federal Trade Commission finalized an order that bans General Motors and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data with consumer reporting agencies. The finalized order also requires the automaker to be more transparent with its consumers and obtain their explicit consent on certain data collection.
GM said Wednesday that customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings.
A GM spokesperson later stated that third-party sharing is “feature-specific and consent-based, with information shared only as needed to provide requested functionality.” Customers can manage permissions and withdraw consent; however, those who choose not to share certain data may have limited access to related features, while other OnStar services would continue, according to GM.

title_en: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
title_fa: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
excerpt_en: This is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented by AI, but is also a high risk because of AI.
excerpt_fa: This is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented by AI, but is also a high risk because of AI.
content_en:
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites. It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.
The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.
Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.
So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz.
Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post. Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP.
Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help.
Wiz thanked Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Imperva, Microsoft, and Vercel. (While WordPress sites use PHP, WordPress has issued a statement saying that the flaw isn’t WordPress specific, and sites running its CMS must patch their servers and work with their web-hosting companies to ensure their sites are protected.)
OpenAI says that these flaws were found by researchers before hackers discovered them. So there were no reports of exploits in the wild. This is also in part because, before AI, these flaws were too hard for hackers to exploit. “With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts,” Wiz warned in its blog about the flaws.
In other words, this is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented because of AI, but is also a high risk only because of AI.
Now that the issue has been disclosed, hackers are fully in the know. The race is on for the internet to patch tens millions of websites before hackers can attack the unpatched ones. Hence the NSA’s guidance that if you can’t patch your PHP website right away, you’re better off pulling it offline until you can.

title_en: There's a new Apple Music logo and it looks like ripples in water
title_fa: There's a new Apple Music logo and it looks like ripples in water
excerpt_en: Maybe they should use it as the app logo instead.
excerpt_fa: Maybe they should use it as the app logo instead.
content_en:
There's a new Apple Music logo and it looks like ripples in water
This should pair well with the Liquid Glass design language.
Apple just revealed a fairly unique design language and logo for Apple Music. It looks like a musical note floating underneath rippling waves, which should pair well with the Liquid Glass software interface.
The company says it was made via practical effects by etching the logo on the glass floor of a small tank. This tank was then filled with mineral oil and a transparent cover was placed over the logo. Next, Apple used an instrument to play a short series of tones, which caused the oil to ripple. They filmed everything and, well, here we are.
This project was a collaboration between Apple, music producer Fred Again and a company called NEST Acoustics. "For the rebrand of Apple Music, we wanted sound to create the visuals," a narrator says in an introduction video. "How do we take this idea of music and distill it into something visually beautiful? Essentially the idea was to create the perfect sound wave."
Apple has updated the Apple Music app icon in beta 4 pic.twitter.com/hcx1fknpGr
— Andreas Storm (@avstorm) October 13, 2026
The motion-filled rippling logo will be used at the beginning of Apple Music videos and stuff like concert footage. The actual app icon is going from red to black-and-white, which has not been a hit with folks on the internet. All of these changes are coming with the company's next software releases, including iOS 27.2 and macOS 27.2.

title_en: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
title_fa: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
excerpt_en: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code more effectively, just announced a $66 million Series C round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
excerpt_fa: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code more effectively, just announced a $66 million Series C round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
content_en:
Blacksmith, a platform that helps companies more efficiently build and test software, including code written by AI, announced Wednesday a $66 million Series C funding round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.
In announcing the round, Blacksmith co-founder and CEO Aditya Jayaprakash said the company was founded to make continuous integration (CI) — the process of building, testing, merging, and validating code changes — “less painful.” In a blog post, he said that “most companies are struggling to keep up with the volume of CI they need to run,” especially in an era where so much code is written by AI.
“As agents write more of the world’s software, the question that matters is whether it can be trusted,” he added.
The company also announced that its annual recurring revenue has grown 17x and that it has run over 90 million CI jobs, or individual automated code checks. Customers include Mercury and Granola.
The Series C comes just two months after its $45 million Series B, which valued the company at $550 million. A year ago, Blacksmith was valued at $60 million after raising a $10 million Series A. It has raised $125 million to date.

title_en: Waymo starts offering rides at the Las Vegas airport
title_fa: Waymo starts offering rides at the Las Vegas airport
excerpt_en: Waymo only just started offering rides to the public in Las Vegas in September but is already serving a 24-square-mile area in the city.
excerpt_fa: Waymo only just started offering rides to the public in Las Vegas in September but is already serving a 24-square-mile area in the city.
content_en:
Waymo is now shuttling customers to and from the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, with pickups and drop-offs happening at dedicated “autonomous vehicle zones” at Terminal 1 and Terminal 3, the company announced Wednesday.
This is the sixth major airport that Waymo is serving. The company already offers rides at Phoenix Sky Harbor, Nashville International, San Antonio International, San Francisco International, and San José International airports.
Waymo only just started offering rides to the public in Las Vegas in September but is already serving a 24-square-mile area in the city. The company said the rides to and from the Las Vegas airport will be limited at first to just a few riders, before opening up to all customers.
Amazon-owned Zoox already offers rides at the Vegas airport, and more robotaxis are coming to Sin City. In August, state regulators approved permits that will allow Tesla and Uber to put thousands of them on the city’s streets in the next year.

title_en: Sony's PlayStation Pulse headset arrives on November 19 for $100
title_fa: Sony's PlayStation Pulse headset arrives on November 19 for $100
excerpt_en: Pre-orders open on October 29.
excerpt_fa: Pre-orders open on October 29.
content_en:
Sony's PlayStation Pulse headset arrives on November 19 for $100
Pre-orders open on October 29.
Sony has revealed when you can get your hands on its PlayStation Pulse wireless headset. The cans will ship on November 19 in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and more than a dozen other countries. Pre-orders open on October 29. Availability in other countries will be announced later.
The headset, which is available in white and midnight black, costs $100. That seems fairly reasonable at a time when pretty much everything is getting more expensive. It costs $50 less than the PlayStation Pulse Elite, Sony's first planar magnetic headset.
The PlayStation Pulse has larger planar magnetic drivers than those found on the previous model. Sony says this allows the headset to deliver "fuller, deeper bass, while keeping the clean sounds players have enjoyed from Pulse Elite." The company added that the spatial accuracy offered by the drivers helps folks pick up on directional cues while playing games. The mic, meanwhile, has "AI-enhanced noise rejection" to minimize background sounds.
The headset offers Bluetooth connectivity as well as the PlayStation Link protocol, which connects it to supported devices such as the PS5, PlayStation Portal, Mac and PC. The tech is said to offer seamless switching between connected devices and lossless, ultra-low latency audio.
A higher-end model called the Pulse Edge is set to arrive in 2027. Sony will start shipping its $220 Pulse Elevate wireless speakers, which also have planar magnetic drivers, next month.

title_en: Supernatural's VR exercise app has relaunched on Meta VR headsets
title_fa: Supernatural's VR exercise app has relaunched on Meta VR headsets
excerpt_en: It's in early access and subscriptions cost $20 per month or $200 each year.
excerpt_fa: It's in early access and subscriptions cost $20 per month or $200 each year.
content_en:
Supernatural's VR exercise app has relaunched on Meta VR headsets
It's in early access and subscriptions cost $20 per month or $200 each year.
The VR fitness app Supernatural has returned to Meta headsets as an early access release. This is welcome news for fans of the platform, as Meta paused new content for the exercise app earlier this year. It has relaunched as an independent entity.
The new Supernatural costs $20 per month or $200 a year, which was the original subscription price when the software first launched back in 2020. The team promises new workouts every week, with many "back-catalog favorites" returning in the "weeks and months ahead." The first batch of new workouts arrives at the end of the month.
"It's not every day you get to make a comeback, but thanks to the Supernatural community, that's exactly what we're doing," said CEO James Senior.
The early access release already features thousands of workouts, including a bunch of remastered favorites. There are hundreds of music tracks to choose from and a brand-new virtual environment based on a glacial lake. Up to four people in a single household can share a headset, which should lead to some friendly competition. Returning members also can transfer pre-existing points, badges and fitness streaks.
The company is working on rebuilding the real-time workout platform, which lets people exercise with friends online. That won't be available for a while, as it's currently in a testing phase. It's also making a mobile companion app that tracks fitness progress. Finally, there will be even more virtual environments added to the lineup in the coming weeks.
Supernatural and Beat Saber were pretty much the killer apps for VR in the early 2020s. It's good to see they are both still going strong.

title_en: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises
title_fa: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises
excerpt_en: Trying to fill a OnePlus-shaped hole, Oppo plays it a little safe.
excerpt_fa: Trying to fill a OnePlus-shaped hole, Oppo plays it a little safe.
content_en:
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises
Trying to fill a OnePlus-shaped hole, Oppo plays it a little safe.
Oppo returns with another flagship phone with telephoto accessories and impressive specs. The Find X10 Pro Max is launching across Europe, Asia and other territories, supplanting last year's Find X9 Pro and sitting below the Find X9 Ultra. However, if you're based in the US, it will once again be hard to get the company's newest phone.
Oppo isn't breaking much new ground this year with its upper-midrange Find X10 series. Those changes include some minor design tweaks. Aside from a standalone color sensor and flash positioned next to the camera unit, it looks like another Find X series 'pro' phone. The company seems to have kept the Find X10 design separate from last year's Ultra and Find N6 foldable with its circular camera design. A slender orange accent outlines the camera array, the latest nod to Oppo's collaboration with Hasselblad.
The materials and finish are further refined, with a matte-finish aluminum frame and a textured back panel that's actually quite smooth. (I thought it would be grippier!) The mid-flagship comes in Luna White (the phone I tested) and Titanium Grey, which has a smooth back cover that lacks the aforementioned textured panel.
The Find X10 Pro Max has a 6.78-inch display, roughly the same as the X9 Ultra, peaking at 3,600 nits. It's noticeably brighter than the Find X9 Pro. It also supports adaptive refresh rates from 1 to 144Hz, plus 10-bit color depth and Dolby Vision.
Oppo is keen to highlight the refinements it made to color temperature adjustments on the display, with faster changes in ambient light levels and a new "adaptive tone" option that uses a new five-channel sensor to better match the surrounding light. I couldn't particularly discern the difference in color changes. Still, auto-brightness seemed snappier when switching between dark rooms and bright outdoor daylight, which is crucial when trying to grab quick shots of a drone I was also testing at the time.
Cameras are still Oppo's smartphone obsession, though it gets a little confusing this time around. Its newest smartphone's cameras arguably aren't quite as potent as the company's flagship, the Find X9 Ultra, which launched only a few months ago.
That all comes down to the sensors. The Find X10 Pro Max comes with three (different) 200-megapixel sensors on the main, telephoto and ultrawide cameras. However, the Find X9 Ultra featured a significantly larger 1/1.12-inch main camera sensor from Sony. Meanwhile, the Find X10 Pro Max shifted to a 1/1.3-inch Samsung HPC sensor, making the X9 Ultra's main sensor roughly 25 percent larger. When I compared the phones' images, the X9 Ultra handled low light better, especially in Hasselblad Master mode, which strips away computational photography augmentations.
On that note, there's also a new "Lumo True" image engine for natural color, tones and textures, which minimizes aggressive AI processing, and that bears out. Compared with the X9 Pro and Ultra, the X10 Pro Max makes fewer computational guesses on text detail and patterning from excessive AI correction.
The Find X10 Pro Max's telephoto camera can reach 3x optical zoom, then crop into the massive 200MP sensor to extend that range to 6x lossless zoom. It doesn't approach the heady 10x zoom of the Find X9 Ultra, though. The Find X10 Pro Max is better equipped for macro photography, however, as it's capable of a 10cm focal distance on its 3x periscope telephoto lens.
More broadly, when pitted against the Find X9 Pro, I was pleasantly surprised to see that this year's X10 Pro Max autofocuses better in low light and captures more detail, regardless of the shooting mode I used.
The Find X10 series' default setup will process full-res 200MP images into 26MP images across its entire zoom range, which is a nice touch and means less fussing around in the settings. Naturally, you can choose a high-res shooting mode if you want every single pixel.
There are plenty of features for video power users, too. Oppo claims its new DeepPix technology, which is built into Samsung's ISOCELL HPC sensor, delivers up to 17 stops of dynamic range, helping it capture in both bright and dimly lit environments. I didn't notice substantial dynamic range improvements in stills, but the technology is aimed more at video, preserving detail in high-contrast scenes.
The Find X10 Pro seems less prone to blown-out footage in bright light, but early testing suggests incremental improvement rather than a headline feature. If you're a vlogger or dedicated smartphone videographer, you'll appreciate the slight upgrade here, although many may not even notice it.
Those video pros have plenty of other modes to play with, too. The X10 Pro Max's Pro Video mode offers open-gate capture, using each sensor's full imaging area for wider coverage and giving editors more latitude to crop and reframe footage in post-production. It also supports Oppo's O-Log2 format, LUT previewing and support for Blackmagic's camera app. If you're going all-in, Oppo also teamed up with Tilta for a KHRONOS creator kit, with a phone cage, grip, cooling fan and flash.
The teleconvertor system makes a return and feels less flimsy this time around. Composed of a specialized case, teleconvertor lens (which looks like a silencer for a pistol) and lens plate, it's a fun (optional) addition to the Find X10 Pro Max's camera offering.
The teleconvertor lens itself is the same as the Find X9 Pro's, but you will need a new adapter plate and case for the Find X10 Pro Max. With the Find X9 Pro, the telephoto lens plate that slides onto the felt a little too much like an early prototype. Over time, the black finish also scraped off after repeated removal, which had to be done often because the plate obscured the other camera sensors.

That all comes down to the sensors. The Find X10 Pro Max comes with three (different) 200-megapixel sensors on the main, telephoto and ultrawide cameras. However, the Find X9 Ultra featured a significantly larger 1/1.12-inch main camera sensor from Sony. Meanwhile, the Find X10 Pro Max shifted to a 1/1.3-inch Samsung HPC sensor, making the X9 Ultra's main sensor roughly 25 percent larger. When I compared the phones' images, the X9 Ultra handled low light better, especially in Hasselblad Master mode, which strips away computational photography augmentations.
On that note, there's also a new "Lumo True" image engine for natural color, tones and textures, which minimizes aggressive AI processing, and that bears out. Compared with the X9 Pro and Ultra, the X10 Pro Max makes fewer computational guesses on text detail and patterning from excessive AI correction.
The Find X10 Pro Max's telephoto camera can reach 3x optical zoom, then crop into the massive 200MP sensor to extend that range to 6x lossless zoom. It doesn't approach the heady 10x zoom of the Find X9 Ultra, though. The Find X10 Pro Max is better equipped for macro photography, however, as it's capable of a 10cm focal distance on its 3x periscope telephoto lens.
More broadly, when pitted against the Find X9 Pro, I was pleasantly surprised to see that this year's X10 Pro Max autofocuses better in low light and captures more detail, regardless of the shooting mode I used.
The Find X10 series' default setup will process full-res 200MP images into 26MP images across its entire zoom range, which is a nice touch and means less fussing around in the settings. Naturally, you can choose a high-res shooting mode if you want every single pixel.
There are plenty of features for video power users, too. Oppo claims its new DeepPix technology, which is built into Samsung's ISOCELL HPC sensor, delivers up to 17 stops of dynamic range, helping it capture in both bright and dimly lit environments. I didn't notice substantial dynamic range improvements in stills, but the technology is aimed more at video, preserving detail in high-contrast scenes.
The Find X10 Pro seems less prone to blown-out footage in bright light, but early testing suggests incremental improvement rather than a headline feature. If you're a vlogger or dedicated smartphone videographer, you'll appreciate the slight upgrade here, although many may not even notice it.
Those video pros have plenty of other modes to play with, too. The X10 Pro Max's Pro Video mode offers open-gate capture, using each sensor's full imaging area for wider coverage and giving editors more latitude to crop and reframe footage in post-production. It also supports Oppo's O-Log2 format, LUT previewing and support for Blackmagic's camera app. If you're going all-in, Oppo also teamed up with Tilta for a KHRONOS creator kit, with a phone cage, grip, cooling fan and flash.
The teleconvertor system makes a return and feels less flimsy this time around. Composed of a specialized case, teleconvertor lens (which looks like a silencer for a pistol) and lens plate, it's a fun (optional) addition to the Find X10 Pro Max's camera offering.
The teleconvertor lens itself is the same as the Find X9 Pro's, but you will need a new adapter plate and case for the Find X10 Pro Max. With the Find X9 Pro, the telephoto lens plate that slides onto the felt a little too much like an early prototype. Over time, the black finish also scraped off after repeated removal, which had to be done often because the plate obscured the other camera sensors.
The new lens mounting plate sadly has the same issue: It covers those other 200MP sensors when you use the...

title_en: Now you can chat with Gemini while using Google Maps through CarPlay
title_fa: Now you can chat with Gemini while using Google Maps through CarPlay
excerpt_en: Just tap the new Gemini icon to get started.
excerpt_fa: Just tap the new Gemini icon to get started.
content_en:
Now you can chat with Gemini while using Google Maps through CarPlay
Just tap the new Gemini icon to get started.
If you're one of the many CarPlay users who prefers Google Maps for navigation, Google has begun rolling out a small but meaningful update for the iOS version of Maps. Now you can use the company's conversational driving experience, Gemini in navigation, through CarPlay. With Maps open, you'll see a new Gemini icon toward the bottom right of the interface. Just tap the bottom to start asking questions of the company's chatbot.
"It's a conversational way to find stops on-the-go, report traffic disruptions, get information about places, and more," Google explains, adding Gemini is particularly adept at answering multi-part questions like "what park is famous for gorgeous views overlooking the city?" Gemini in navigation is starting to roll out today to CarPlay users in the US and throughout the world. As always, it may take a few days before the update arrives on your device, so be patient if you don't see it right away.
The update arrives after Google yesterday announced it was beginning to roll out Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto users. When enabled, the feature allows the chatbot to pull information from your other Google apps to personalize its responses. In practice, Google says Personal Intelligence improves Gemini's reasoning capabilities makes the assistant capable of delivering more specific details as they relate to your questions and prompts.

title_en: A permanent Pokémon store will open in London, with more locations outside Asia to follow
title_fa: A permanent Pokémon store will open in London, with more locations outside Asia to follow
excerpt_en: The new retail location is set to open by 2029.
excerpt_fa: The new retail location is set to open by 2029.
content_en:
A permanent Pokémon store will open in London, with more locations outside Asia to follow
The new retail location is set to open by 2029.
As it stands, Pokémon fans outside of Asia either have to travel to the continent or hope for a pop-up closer to home if they want to spend (probably lots of) money at one of the brand's physical retail locations. That's changing, though, as The Pokémon Company says it's opening several permanent stores outside of Asia. The first of those will be in London and it's slated to open by 2029.
Pop-up Pokémon shops have appeared in London in the past, including one at the Natural History Museum earlier this year and others during various editions of the Pokémon European International Championships. As with the pop-ups, the permanent location will have exclusive merch.
"We are always exploring new opportunities that help us create unique and memorable experiences for our fans," Gaku Susai, The Pokémon Company International's chief product and experience officer said. "This new London store will give visitors the chance to step into the world of Pokémon, whether they're discovering the brand for the first time or have been Trainers for years."
The Pokémon Company said it will reveal details about other physical locations in the future. If it ends up bringing a store to New York, that wouldn't be its first one in the city. Pokémon Center New York opened in 2001. Four years later, that location was turned into Nintendo's flagship physical store.

title_en: Foursquare co-founder says equity holders saw no returns from the company’s acquisition
title_fa: Foursquare co-founder says equity holders saw no returns from the company’s acquisition
excerpt_en: Foursquare raised $411 million in funding according to PitchBook data, but its equity holders saw no returns from its final acquisition.
excerpt_fa: Foursquare raised $411 million in funding according to PitchBook data, but its equity holders saw no returns from its final acquisition.
content_en:
Last month, advertising company Infillion acquired location-data platform Foursquare, a once popular social network, at an undisclosed value. Now, in a new blog post, Foursquare co-founder and former CEO Dennis Crowley said that investors didn’t see any returns from the sale.
Crowley referenced a post by an angel investor, inferred that neither preferred nor common stockholders got any value out of the deal, and said he was disappointed by the outcome.
“I was heartbroken by this ending. So many people put so much time and energy and passion and love into building Foursquare — the company, the products, the brand, the culture. If you were part of it (or even close to it), you know exactly what I’m talking about. To our ~1600 former employees over 17 years, I am sorry the Foursquare story ended in such a way that makes it seem like our collective efforts were worth … nothing?” he said in the post.
Crowley said that the company did well after it started focusing on enterprise business and had consecutive years with over $100 million in revenue. In 2019, the company raised capital from a private equity firm and in 2021 brought in the banker who led the raise as CEO. Crowley blamed the final outcome on that transition, saying that the management of the company wasn’t able to preserve or create new value.
Foursquare, which had raised over $411 million in funding according to PitchBook data, eventually shut down its app in 2024.
Several people reacted to Crowley’s post and said that Foursquare was very useful to them in discovering new places in their cities and also gave ideas for new apps. After Foursquare, startups like Zenly and Jagat, along with Instagram and Snapchat, have explored social maps.
