title_en: What to expect at Apple's 'Pro and Tell' event on October 28
title_fa: What to expect at Apple's 'Pro and Tell' event on October 28
excerpt_en: From the first touchscreen MacBook to an OLED iPad mini, here's everything Apple is expected to announce next week.
excerpt_fa: From the first touchscreen MacBook to an OLED iPad mini, here's everything Apple is expected to announce next week.
content_en:
What to expect at Apple's 'Pro and Tell' event on October 28
From the first touchscreen MacBook to an OLED iPad mini, here's everything Apple is expected to announce next week.
Following the launch of the HomeView and other smart home products last week, Apple has now confirmed its third product event of the season. Invitations bearing the tagline "Pro and Tell" went out this week, and the showcase will take place on October 28 in Los Angeles. However, it won't be a traditional event, but rather a briefing for the press and creators. As usual, Apple doesn't reveal in advance which products it will announce, but all signs point to two main categories: Mac and iPad. If the rumors are true, we'll see the first MacBook with an OLED display and touchscreen, and the M6 chip coming to more Macs. In addition, the iPad mini might also get a major update with an OLED display and a faster chip. Here's everything to expect from next week's event.
A MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen
The star of the show is expected to be a new MacBook Pro, which will is supposed to be the first Mac with a touchscreen. Rumors suggest it will come in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes like the current models — but they may end up looking quite different. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman recently reported that this new MacBook could be thinner and lighter, while the OLED display should allow for thinner bezels and a hole-punch camera cutout with a Dynamic Island instead of a notch. Chances are this will be the biggest redesign of the MacBook Pro since the versions that were introduced in 2021.
However, don't expect to see the new M6 chip inside it. Gurman's sources claimed that Apple will stick with the current M5 Pro and M5 Max, rather than switching to the M6 family. If you were hoping for a faster MacBook Pro, you'll likely have to wait until 2027, when Apple is rumored to refresh its high-end laptop with the M7 Pro and M7 Max chips. This Mac won't come cheap either, according to a report by Macworld. It probably won't be a successor to existing models, but rather an even more expensive version that expands the lineup. The current models without touchscreens should remain available for those not wanting to pay the higher price.
M6 chips come to more Macs
Although the touchscreen MacBook won't get the M6 chip, other Macs will. The M6 was introduced in August with the latest Mac mini, and now other Macs are rumored to be getting it as well. The leading candidate is the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro — Apple did something similar last year with the M5 version. Don't expect a touchscreen, OLED display or any design changes in this version, though. The only upgrade should be the M6 chip, which offers improved performance and lower power consumption.
The iMac is also a strong candidate for an update next week, especially since the current model was introduced in 2024 and still runs on the M4 chip. Here, the M6 chip is expected to mark an even more significant jump, with much better CPU and GPU performance. The M6 also comes with a dual 16-core Neural Engine, which runs AI tasks much faster. We may also see new color options available, although the design will remain the same.
An iPad mini with OLED
Macs likely won't be the only products getting an update at next week's event. The iPad mini is also expected to get some spotlight with a new generation, and this will be a big one, too. Apple is reportedly adding an OLED display to the iPad mini for the first time. Current models still have LCD screens. If true, the mini will be the first iPad besides the iPad Pro to feature an OLED display.
Another upgrade should be the A20 Pro chip, which is already in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Currently, the iPad mini still runs on the A17 Pro chip from the iPhone 15 Pro — and is known for heating up a lot. Other rumors about the new iPad mini include thinner bezels around the screen, a relocated front-facing camera and some level of water resistance for the first time. Of course, none of these details have been confirmed yet, so we'll find out what Apple has to share for sure on October 28.

title_en: The latest PlayStation firmware may have already been cracked ahead of GTA 6
title_fa: The latest PlayStation firmware may have already been cracked ahead of GTA 6
excerpt_en: Hackers aren't giving up at cracking the Playstation 5's latest firmware as evidenced by a new video showing an apparent kernel exploit.
excerpt_fa: Hackers aren't giving up at cracking the Playstation 5's latest firmware as evidenced by a new video showing an apparent kernel exploit.
content_en:
The latest PlayStation firmware may have already been cracked ahead of GTA 6
A firmware exploit does not mean the game can be pirated, though.
Sony's latest PlayStation 5 firmware (14.10.00) appears to have been cracked, based on a video shared by a developer named "Gezine" on X. The video shows Gezine navigating through the PS5's hidden Debug Settings, menus that are typically only available if you have kernel-level access to the console's operating system.
A possible exploit for the PS5's latest firmware is notable both because Sony released the software update in October, and because the firmware is reportedly necessary to play the year's biggest release. According to datamining by X account PlayStation Game Size, Grand Theft Auto VI requires the latest firmware to run, theoretically blocking it from being played on jailbroken consoles running older firmware. It was possible to jailbreak the console and play illegally obtained copies of games using the "Relapse" jailbreak on earlier PS5 firmware, but the update to 14.10 closed that loophole — until now.
Hello 14.10 pic.twitter.com/D7prKmOkbD
— Gezine (@gezine_dev) October 19, 2026
Of course, just because a developer has found a kernel exploit for the console's firmware doesn't mean GTA VI itself is any closer to being ripped or ported to another platform. Gezine has not publicly shared their method for hacking the PS5's firmware. In fact, in a reply to their original post sharing the video of the console's debug menus, they said they were "gonna ask for disclosure later," suggesting they may report it to a bug bounty program first. Sony hasn't acknowledged this hack, but the company does run a bug bounty program that pays security researchers for identifying similar ones.
A kernel exploit is also only one of the ingredients necessary to "unlock" a digital game for use elsewhere. A new hypervisor exploit — a hack of the software security layer running under the kernel — would be necessary to crack games or run other illegal copies. At least so far, that exploit hasn't materialized. Without it, Grand Theft Auto VI will only be available through a traditional physical or digital purchase. And, unlike with past games, even physically purchasing the new GTA only gets you a download code and a game box. The game's console exclusivity, at least for now, is one reason players might be interested in playing a cracked version. The more obvious reason is to avoid paying $80.

title_en: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
title_fa: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
excerpt_en: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of...
excerpt_fa: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of...
content_en:
Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter’s third quarter earnings call Tuesday.
Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
Musk called the merger “a good idea,” though he cautioned it wasn’t a guarantee.
Musk called the merger “a good idea,” though he cautioned it wasn’t a guarantee.
Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions.
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. “So it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation.”
The groups have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction — and there’s no guarantee that they will. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he continued. “And particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.”
That said, Musk called the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger a “good idea.” He continued:
I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity. And there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the TeraFab, obviously robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity. So I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies. They’ve got to come up with something and then that’s going to be put to the shareholders as a vote.
A Tesla-SpaceX merger would be a blockbuster corporate deal creating a mega-entity valued upwards of $3.6 trillion. But combining Musk’s car and energy company with his AI and rocket company would not be without its tradeoffs. A lot depends on which company absorbs the other. To buy SpaceX, Tesla would have to create millions of new stock shares, which for current Tesla owners would mean owning a smaller slice of a much larger pie. SpaceX’s launch goals require tens of billions of dollars every year — extra spending that could drain Tesla’s ability to build new car factories and battery plants.
That said, most Wall Street analysts and legal experts believe SpaceX would acquire Tesla (or absorb it through a stock swap) rather than vice versa. Since its IPO, SpaceX has maintained a higher valuation than Tesla. A merger in that direction would allow SpaceX shareholders to hold the majority control of the combined mega-entity. Some Tesla shareholders may balk at this deal.
But it would also create one company for those who believe in Musk’s vision of the future — robot cars, humanoid robots, AI super-intelligence, and human habitats on Mars — in which to place their investments. And Tesla shareholder approved Musk’s enormous pay package last year — even after a Delaware judge tossed it over lack of independence.
Earlier this month, Barclays published a client note suggesting a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination could be announced ahead of Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting scheduled for December 3, 2026.

title_en: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
title_fa: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
excerpt_en: Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor, even as its infrastructure spending balloons ahead of a planned November IPO.
excerpt_fa: Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor, even as its infrastructure spending balloons ahead of a planned November IPO.
content_en:
Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal.
The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which include deals still in negotiation.
And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers.
Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during that same time period, with only two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales, according to the WSJ report.
Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage.
Last week, the company told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue alone has now reached $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

title_en: ChatGPT now lets you lock sensitive chats behind a PIN
title_fa: ChatGPT now lets you lock sensitive chats behind a PIN
excerpt_en: OpenAI has introduced a new "locked chats" feature to protect users' more sensitive conversations with ChatGPT.
excerpt_fa: OpenAI has introduced a new "locked chats" feature to protect users' more sensitive conversations with ChatGPT.
content_en:
ChatGPT now lets you lock sensitive chats behind a PIN
Locked chats aren't a form of end-to-end encryption, however.
OpenAI is making it easier to protect your ChatGPT conversations from prying eyes with the introduction of a feature called locked chats. With it enabled, you can decide whether a past exchange appears in your regular chat history, pinned chats and conversation search. To access your locked chats, you'll need to input a 4-digit PIN. On an iPhone or Android phone, you can also use authentication systems like Face ID to access those conversations. Either way, you'll find your private conversations grouped under a new project titled "Locked chats."
OpenAI envisions locked chats mostly as a way to prevent people in public or someone you hand your phone to from seeing your conversations with ChatGPT. What they aren't is a form of end-to-end encryption or a way to skirt OpenAI's legal obligations if you get in trouble with your workplace or the law. The company says so explicitly in a newly published support page, where it also notes locked chats won't automatically change your model training settings, or how long OpenAI retains your private conversations. That said, if you need to reset your account PIN for any reason, doing so will delete all of your locked chats, alongside any files you've uploaded to their project space. "This cannot be undone, and OpenAI Support cannot recover the deleted content," the company warns.
OpenAI says it's rolling out locked chats to users gradually. If you don't see the option right away, it may take a few days before it arrives in your account. Availability will extend to free accounts, as well as to those with Go, Plus and Pro subscriptions. On Android and iOS, you can use voice mode in combination with locked chats, though you can't lock your Codex conversations behind the feature.

title_en: SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
title_fa: SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
excerpt_en: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company would attempt to catch Starship and its booster next month, with the goal of recovering the entire orbital launch system for the first time. If successful, Musk said, the attempt would mark the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle...
excerpt_fa: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company would attempt to catch Starship and its booster next month, with the goal of recovering the entire orbital launch system for the first time. If successful, Musk said, the attempt would mark the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle...
content_en:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company would attempt to catch Starship and its booster next month, with the goal of recovering the entire orbital launch system for the first time. If successful, Musk said, the attempt would mark the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered.
SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
If successful, it would be the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered.
If successful, it would be the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered.
“This is a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization consciousness,” he said during the company’s third quarter earnings report Tuesday.
But he also allowed for the possibility of a failure. “Success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I’d say it’s more likely than not that this succeeds next flight,” Musk said. “And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year and then accelerating next year.”
“Success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I’d say it’s more likely than not that this succeeds next flight.”
— Elon MuskStarship is a two-stage system, composed of the Super Heavy booster (first stage) and the Starship spacecraft (second stage). It stands approximately 120 meters (around 400 feet) tall with a 9-meter diameter, and is powered by SpaceX’s Raptor engines burning liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Starship, which was first introduced in 2018, was designed to return to the launch site, where launch towers with mechanical “chopstick” arms catch the vehicle mid-air.
Last month’s Starship launch represented two firsts for its next gen rocket: send the spacecraft into Earth orbit, and insert a few dozen of SpaceX’s larger and more capable V3 satellites into the Starlink constellation for the first time. Still, the launch wasn’t without its snafus: one Raptor engine shut down prematurely during ascent, prompting mission control to adapt and complete the climb on remaining. Because of the issue, SpaceX cut the planned 10-hour, 6-orbit mission short after about 3 hours and 2 Earth orbits.
The Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico, while the Starship upper stage executed a de-orbit burn and ended with a fiery vertical splashdown in the Pacific Ocean north of Hawaii. Neither piece was recovered.

title_en: Judge tosses sexual abuse lawsuit from Sam Altman's sister
title_fa: Judge tosses sexual abuse lawsuit from Sam Altman's sister
excerpt_en: A lawsuit brought by the OpenAI CEO's sister was dismissed after Anne Altman refused a medical exam.
excerpt_fa: A lawsuit brought by the OpenAI CEO's sister was dismissed after Anne Altman refused a medical exam.
content_en:
Judge tosses sexual abuse lawsuit from Sam Altman's sister
The case was dismissed over a refused medical exam, not on the merits.
A federal judge dismissed Ann Altman's lawsuit against her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, on Tuesday. US District Judge Zachary Bluestone didn't rule on the merits of her claims. Instead, he wrote that Ann refused to appear for an independent medical examination, despite being warned that skipping it would lead to the case's dismissal.
Ann Altman filed the lawsuit in January 2025, accusing Sam of sexually abusing her when she was a child. She alleged that the abuse took place at the family's Missouri home between 1997 and 2006, beginning when she was three and he was 12. She said the last instance of alleged abuse took place when her brother was an adult.
The case had already been revised once. In March, Bluestone ruled that Ann's original sexual assault and battery claims had expired years earlier. But the judge allowed her to refile under a Missouri childhood sexual abuse law. She then filed the amended suit that was dismissed on Tuesday.
The OpenAI CEO, now 41, has denied the claims. Bluestone also reportedly approved Sam Altman's request on Tuesday to withdraw a defamation counterclaim he made against his sister.
In a joint statement made after Ann Altman's initial lawsuit was filed, Sam Altman, his mother and two younger brothers called the allegations "entirely untrue." They claimed that Ann Altman had "mental health challenges" and "refuses conventional treatment and lashes out at family members who are genuinely trying to help."
Ann Altman's former lawyer, Santos Perez, who withdrew from the case in October, wrote in a statement, "I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie."

title_en: Netflix is telling investors not to worry, even though you’re watching less and less
title_fa: Netflix is telling investors not to worry, even though you’re watching less and less
excerpt_en: Netflix is making monetization a top priority amid reports of falling viewing time. As part of its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday, Netflix lists improvements to monetization as one of its main focuses going forward, alongside efforts to boost entertainment value and...
excerpt_fa: Netflix is making monetization a top priority amid reports of falling viewing time. As part of its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday, Netflix lists improvements to monetization as one of its main focuses going forward, alongside efforts to boost entertainment value and...
content_en:
Netflix is making monetization a top priority amid reports of falling viewing time. As part of its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday, Netflix lists improvements to monetization as one of its main focuses going forward, alongside efforts to boost entertainment value and leverage new technology.
Netflix is telling investors not to worry, even though you’re watching less and less
Improving monetization is one of Netflix’s top priorities.
Improving monetization is one of Netflix’s top priorities.
The streaming giant doesn’t say exactly how it plans to improve its monetization, but the company notes that these goals will help Netflix “create member value that lets us occasionally raise prices, and increase advertiser demand.” Netflix also highlighted plans to push further into original titles, live events, and third-party programming as it faces an “intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention.”
An analysis from financial firm Jefferies estimated that Netflix’s monthly viewing time per member dropped to 49 hours in the first half of this year, down from 66 hours in the first half of 2023, according to a report from Reuters. At the same time, Netflix made up 7.8 percent of US viewing time in the US in July, a one-percentage-point dip from the same time last year, The New York Times reports.
During an earnings call, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos pointed to success abroad when answering a question about the company’s content strategy. “We see titles across Latin America, EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia-Pacific), driving engagement, subscriber growth, revenue, and profit,” Sarandos said. “Now, the US is also working. It’s just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like.”
Last week, Netflix laid off around 1,000 employees, while replacing key executives, including chief content officer Bela Bajaria and film head Dan Lin. Former Disney executive Peter Rice is taking over as chief content officer on October 26th. The Wall Street Journal recently reported that Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos complained internally that US-based users have been spending less time on the service, and that it’s “short on new hit shows.”
In its letter to investors, Netflix mentions its upcoming lineup of NFL games, its Grand Theft Auto VI preview, and its partnership with French TV station TF1 as evidence of opening its platform to a wider breadth of content. The company reported earning $12.9 billion over the past few months, marking a 12 percent year-over-year increase. It also plans to bring its ad-supported tier — which raked in $1.5 billion last year — to 15 new countries in 2027.
In the coming months, Netflix may be facing tougher competition from HBO Max and Paramount Plus following the Skydance megamerger, as co-CEO David Ellison has said that he plans to combine the two apps into a single service. The streamer struck deals with several creators as it competes with YouTube, which has reportedly offered channels “millions of dollars” not to post their videos on Netflix.
Netflix has also weighed making even bigger changes to its app, including integrating other third-party streamers, such as Peacock and Fox One, as well as adding always-on channels, according to reports from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal.
Update, October 20th: Added a quote from Sarandos.

title_en: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
title_fa: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
excerpt_en: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.
excerpt_fa: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.
content_en:
SpaceX’s data centers and Grok agents were more profitable than investors expected in the third quarter of the year, as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on artificial intelligence, which now makes up 52% of its income.
CEO Elon Musk’s deep tech conglomerate reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to its regulatory filing.
That number was driven by growth in all segments, but especially its renamed “Super Intelligence” business line, which generated $7.5 billion in revenue from the recently acquired Cursor coding tool, Grok bot, and most importantly, the company’s burgeoning neocloud business, which now boasts 1.7 GW of compute. The AI business generated $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition.
The top-line revenue number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income that might be attributed to a SpaceX investment in another company.
The growing revenue is balanced against total capital expenditures of $19.6 billion, as SpaceX continues to build out a second data center project, Colossus II, and increase investment in Starship, the heavy-lift rocket it sees as vital to deploying a new generation of Starlink satellites and developing orbital data centers. CFO Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter.
During a livestreamed discussion of the results with investors, Musk said he was spending four days a week in Memphis, Tennessee, the site of Colossus II, working to bring the data center online.
“People are starting to realize [that] the constraint on deployment of super intelligence is more in power and cooling and infrastructure than it is in chips,” Musk argued, saying that he had tasked a team of SpaceX engineers to solve that problem. “This is a bit like the New York Yankees playing in Little League. It’s not fair, but the net result is being able to deploy power cooling infrastructure at a rate that is vastly faster than any anyone else.”
In one example, Musk noted that manufacturers of turbines to power data centers are facing 12- to 18-month delays in obtaining the metals that blades and vanes required for those machines. Now, SpaceX is using the metal casting capabilities developed for SpaceX to make those components and obtain turbines more quickly.
Musk also said that the next test flight of the Starship rocket, expected in November, would see SpaceX attempt to recover both the first-stage booster and the second stage. Recovering both segments of the vehicle would be a “massive technology milestone,” Musk said, but the true milestone will be reflying both stages.
SpaceX also saw growth in subscribers to its Starlink space internet network, reaching 13.6 million consumers, with Musk predicting that the growth of AI agents would lead to more demand for connectivity.
Despite those capital expenditures, the company’s revenue boost was substantial enough to push it back into profitability. SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion, a turnaround from the $1 billion loss in the same quarter last year. It will still have some catching up to do if it wants to remain profitable for the year, however. In the first nine months of the year, SpaceX still had a net income loss of $413 million.
Musk took a particularly bullish stance on the company’s Super Intelligence business segment, predicting that SpaceX’s annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 will be “somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion.”
More concretely, Johnsen forecast total revenue for the first quarter of 2027 in the range of $33 billion to $37 billion.
This is a developing story. TechCrunch will update.

More concretely, Johnsen forecast total revenue for the first quarter of 2027 in the range of $33 billion to $37 billion.
This is a developing story. TechCrunch will update.

excerpt_fa: OpenAI says it's adding Orchestra's team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results.
content_en:
OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company announced on its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC.
Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug-discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials.
OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna and Novo Nordisk.
The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma. In the startup world, there is an ongoing fear that at any moment, the labs will launch new features and become competitors. In this case, Orchestra is getting absorbed, rather than stomped out.

Snap has a new brand ambassador for its Specs AR glasses: Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr. The company has brought on Downey as Specs’ “Chief Customer Experience Officer” and has published several videos featuring Downey showcasing the capabilities of the new glasses, including as a tool to get help with a putt, practice art, and watch a private video of an MMA match in bed. In one video, he also dumps the contents of a box labeled “AI glasses” into a trash bin — a shot at Meta’s popular smart glasses.

title_en: SpaceX says big AI growth fueled revenue jump
title_fa: SpaceX says big AI growth fueled revenue jump
excerpt_en: SpaceX announced revenues of $14.6 billion in its Q3 earnings on Tuesday, which it says was a growth of 161 percent year-over-year "fueled by our Super Intelligence (SI) segment and accelerated growth in Connectivity." While its Space division posted a $7 million loss in income...
excerpt_fa: SpaceX announced revenues of $14.6 billion in its Q3 earnings on Tuesday, which it says was a growth of 161 percent year-over-year "fueled by our Super Intelligence (SI) segment and accelerated growth in Connectivity." While its Space division posted a $7 million loss in income...
content_en:
SpaceX announced revenues of $14.6 billion in its Q3 earnings on Tuesday, which it says was a growth of 161 percent year-over-year “fueled by our Super Intelligence (SI) segment and accelerated growth in Connectivity.” While its Space division posted a $7 million loss in income from operations, its Connectivity group posted income from operations $2.4 billion and its SI group posted $431 million.
SpaceX says big AI growth fueled revenue jump
SpaceX announced revenues of $7.6 billion for its ‘SI’ business in its Q3 2026 earnings.
SpaceX announced revenues of $7.6 billion for its ‘SI’ business in its Q3 2026 earnings.
The company’s so-called “SI” business saw revenues of $7.6 billion, which were up 830 percent year-over-year, “primarily driven” by “the activation of new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor, and increased Grok adoption across enterprise customers and consumers.” For its Connectivity business, SpaceX reported revenues of $5.2 billion and 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers. Space business revenues were $1.8 billion, up six percent year-over-year.
SpaceX is livestreamed a video of its earnings call on X, where Elon Musk said that SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster next month, that Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, and that its Starlink connectivity business could generate “several hundred billion dollars a year.”
This is the second earnings report from SpaceX after the company’s IPO in June. The earnings follow a busy Q3 for Elon Musk’s rocket, AI, and social media company, which included the official closing of its $60 billion deal to acquire AI coding tool Cursor, the 13th launch of SpaceX’s Starship, and the launch of a new V5 Starlink residential dish.
During the Q2 earnings call, president Gwynne Shotwell described plans to build out a terrestrial mobile network to compete with T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon. In SpaceX’s Q2 earnings, the company also noted that its “connectivity” business, which encompasses Starlink, didn’t have a loss from operations, while its AI and space businesses did.
Tesla, where Musk is also CEO, reports earnings on Wednesday.
Update, October 20th: Added details from the Q3 earnings call.

title_en: Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
title_fa: Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
excerpt_en: Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down. Cardio...
excerpt_fa: Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down. Cardio...
content_en:
Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down. Cardio Effort and automatic VO2 Max (previously known as Cardio Capacity) are available for the Oura Ring Gen 3 and later models, but only to users with an active Oura membership.
Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
The new features help users better understand how the intensity of regular workouts will affect their long-term health.
The new features help users better understand how the intensity of regular workouts will affect their long-term health.
Instead of measuring how fast or far a user went during a run or bike ride, or metrics like calories burned, Cardio Effort measures how hard their cardiovascular system was working during exercise and how long that effort was sustained. Cardio Effort is calculated for individual workouts taking into account both intensity and duration but provides a plain language evaluation that compares a user’s cumulative weekly effort against a personalized baseline.
One one end of the scale is a Light rating that’s described as being a “substantially lower cardiovascular strain than your usual baseline.” The rating scale progresses through Fair, Maintaining, Building, and Reaching at the other end which means your weekly Cardio Effort had a “markedly higher exposure relative to your baseline, signaling that it may be time to prioritize recovery.” So instead of always pushing a user to increase their efforts, the feature does make recommendations for rest when it may be more beneficial.
Oura Rings already support VO2 Max readings that are used to track aerobic capacity, but the previous Cardio Capacity feature was somewhat cumbersome because estimating a user’s maximum oxygen uptake required a six-minute walking test for calibration. The new version, automatic VO2 Max, currently available as a beta feature through Oura Labs, automatically activates after users complete five “qualifying GPS-enabled activities” that include walks, runs, and hikes.
Once activated VO2 Max readings will be available in the Oura app’s My Health Heart Hub section with a user’s current estimate, their capacity rated as low, fair, high, or peak, how their aerobic capacity has changed over time, and personalized insights for when VO2 Max “meaningfully shifts or stays consistent.”

title_en: Meta suspends Muse chats sharing feature after it left private details exposed
title_fa: Meta suspends Muse chats sharing feature after it left private details exposed
excerpt_en: Researchers accessed 6,800 shared conversations with the AI agent, including internal company documents.
excerpt_fa: Researchers accessed 6,800 shared conversations with the AI agent, including internal company documents.
content_en:
Meta suspends Muse chats sharing feature after it left private details exposed
Researchers accessed 6,800 shared conversations with the AI agent.
Meta debuted its Muse agentic AI platform last month and bug hunters have already uncovered a privacy problem. Users would share their Muse conversations by creating a URL, but that feature has been disabled after researchers found that anyone could potentially access those links.
Researchers at security firm Claroc discovered that the links for users' shared Muse chats can be found and accessed via a passive DNS search because all the URLs for sharing had the same domain name and used the conversation's title in the subdomain. Passive DNS are records of how human-readable domains resolve to browser-readable IP addresses, basically acting like a phone book for the Internet.
"Muse names each share's web address after the conversation's own title, and that address is written into public DNS," Claroc explained in a blog post. "One passive-DNS search brings back thousands of them, listed by name, like a table of contents."
The company was able to enumerate 6,800 links for shared Muse chats and view private information from both business and personal applications of the service. The exposed personal details included meeting times with a frontier AI lab, a small-business loan application, a bank fraud alert with partial account details, a company's vacation calendar and other internal company documents.
Ars Technica first reported on Claroc's efforts. In a statement to the publication, Meta said "we've paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered." Claroc also noted that its researchers were unable to open a sampling of the links they had previously accessed following Meta's update.

title_en: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
title_fa: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
excerpt_en: Google is bringing Gemini's Personal Intelligence feature to cars, allowing its AI assistant to draw on information from Gmail, Calendar, Maps, YouTube, and other Google services to deliver more personalized responses while driving.
excerpt_fa: Google is bringing Gemini's Personal Intelligence feature to cars, allowing its AI assistant to draw on information from Gmail, Calendar, Maps, YouTube, and other Google services to deliver more personalized responses while driving.
content_en:
Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
The company said Tuesday it’s upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences.
Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in, software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
The feature will launch in Android Auto, starting today, and expand to cars with Google Built-in in the coming months.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto. Meanwhile, Gemini’s “Personal Intelligence” feature rolled out across the U.S. in March and is now in beta in global markets.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.
Drivers will have to opt in for Personalized Intelligence to work. Once a user does so, they should expect all sorts of cross-pollination. For instance, a driver who is navigating to the airport may be alerted that the flight on their calendar is delayed.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language. Returning to that airport example, a user might ask the AI assistant for their flight gate before quickly following up with a question about whether it’s still on time. Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence. The feature can be turned on or off at any time, and users can selectively choose which apps they’d like to connect, Google said.

title_en: Google brings Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto
title_fa: Google brings Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto
excerpt_en: In the coming months, the feature will also roll out to cars with Google built-in.
excerpt_fa: In the coming months, the feature will also roll out to cars with Google built-in.
content_en:
Google brings Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto
In the coming months, the feature will also roll out to cars with Google built-in.
At the start of the year, Google debuted Personal Intelligence, a Gemini feature that allows the chatbot to pull information from your other Google apps to generate more personalized responses. An expansion in March brought Personal Intelligence to free accounts after it was previously only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. And now Google has begun rolling out the feature to Android Auto users.
In practice, the company says today's update will improve Gemini's reasoning capabilities in cars. It will also make the assistant capable of delivering more specific details as they relate to your questions and prompts. For example, if you're driving to the airport, Google suggests Gemini with Personal Intelligence will be able to answer questions like "what's my flight gate?" and "is my flight on time?" Provided you've linked your Gmail account, it can do all this without you needing to pull over to find a confirmation email.
More broadly, Google says Personal Intelligence makes it easier to interact with Gemini more naturally. For instance, if you need directions to your doctor's office, you can just say "take me to my doctor's appointment," instead of speaking a specific address. Recommendations are also improved. If you're in a new city, Google suggests you can ask for dinner spots along your driving route and Gemini will generate suggestions while factoring in preferences and restrictions, like if you're a vegetarian.
As before, enabling Personal Intelligence is optional, and you can turn it off at any point if you don't want Gemini pulling your data. You can also control what apps Gemini can access. Google is starting to roll out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto users globally starting today (with the exception of those living in Switzerland, the European Economic Area, UK and Nigeria). In the coming months, the company plans to bring the feature to cars with Google built-in too.

title_en: GM to close Detroit battery-assembly plant, but not for reasons you might think
title_fa: GM to close Detroit battery-assembly plant, but not for reasons you might think
excerpt_en: GM is shuttering the Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant, though the closure has nothing to do with the automaker's electrification strategy.
excerpt_fa: GM is shuttering the Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant, though the closure has nothing to do with the automaker's electrification strategy.
content_en:
GM is closing a battery-assembly plant south of Detroit, a spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch.
The Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant assembled battery packs for Cadillac’s flagship EV, the Celestiq, and both electric drive units (the motors that power the car) and battery packs for the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray, a plug-in hybrid version of its famous sports car. Automotive News first reported the closure.
The closure is not related to GM’s electric vehicle strategy, the spokesperson said. Instead, GM leased the site, and the lease was nearing its end.
The employees and work at Brownstown will be moved to other GM facilities, though the company would not confirm which ones.
Like many automakers, GM’s electrification strategy was thrown a curveball after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the sweeping federal law signed last year, repealed incentives to produce and sell EVs.
Since then, the company has pared back its public comments on EVs, though it hasn’t given up on full electrification.
GM continues to produce a range of EVs, including the Chevrolet Silverado EV and the limited-time-only Chevrolet Bolt. It also continues researching new battery chemistries, including lithium-manganese-rich and sodium-ion, and it’s rolling out a new $900 million facility to speed commercialization.

title_en: Employees warned TikTok about child exploitation, court documents show
title_fa: Employees warned TikTok about child exploitation, court documents show
excerpt_en: The company is facing hundreds of lawsuits over its record on safety.
excerpt_fa: The company is facing hundreds of lawsuits over its record on safety.
content_en:
Employees warned TikTok about child exploitation, court documents show
The company is facing hundreds of lawsuits over its record on safety.
Court documents are shedding new light on reported child safety issues at TikTok. According to depositions detailed by NPR, multiple employees repeatedly flagged serious flaws in the company's handling of child safety, including child exploitation, but were "frustrated" with TikTok's response.
The records are drawn from ongoing lawsuits the company is facing related to its handling of child safety. TikTok is the target of hundreds of such lawsuits, though it has settled some cases, including those making claims the app was designed to be be addictive.
According to statements made by company employees, TikTok executives were notified that teens were regularly appearing in live streams in the app, which raised concerns about potential grooming and exploitation. After Forbes published an article in 2022 about teens stripping in TikTok Live videos in which viewers could pay for in-app "gifts," a safety employee said the company knew about such content. Employees also warned that the company was making "significant revenue" from live video content involving children even though TikTok's rules barred minors from appearing in them.
Other employees also flagged shortcomings in the company's parental controls and age-based safety features. For example, a "loophole" allowed minors to bypass TikTok's age checks if they signed up for with a Facebook, Instagram or Google account. The app also contained a "hidden link" that allowed teens to remove themselves from TikTok's "family pairing" feature.
The company didn't provide an on the record statement to NPR. In a statement to Engadget, the company said lawyers had "cherry-picked" the incidents described in the documents. "These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works," a company spokesperson said. "We have invested billions of dollars in Trust & Safety and rolled out more than 50 preset safety, privacy, and security settings for teens, including Family Pairing, which helps parents and guardians customize the experience for their teens. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the well-being of our community."
NPR further cites a report written by Eric Han, TikTok's former head of safety, about the risks posed by algorithmic "rabbit holes" in which the app repeatedly recommends harmful content, like posts related to suicide. The report, which seemingly dates back to 2020, said that there was a "real contagion effect" with such content.
TikTok has recently come under scrutiny for how it's handled repeated recommendations of problematic content. The company introduced a feature in 2021 that was meant to help people avoid "repetitive patterns" of certain types of content. But the company, in an apparent test, held back the feature from millions of users. A teen who was part of that experiment died by suicide after seeing repeated content about self harm, according to documents that have surfaced in a lawsuit brought by New York's attorney general.
Update, Tuesday, October 20, 2026, 7:30PM ET: This post was updated to include a statement from TikTok.

title_en: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
title_fa: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
excerpt_en: Google has joined Amazon in releasing a developer tool that makes it easy for PyTorch users to move their apps off Nvidia GPUs.
excerpt_fa: Google has joined Amazon in releasing a developer tool that makes it easy for PyTorch users to move their apps off Nvidia GPUs.
content_en:
On Tuesday, Google announced that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs.
PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no rewriting of their apps.
Amazon made a similar announcement Monday, when it released its own version of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. TorchNeuron allows AI apps to be ported to Amazon’s homegrown AI chip, Trainium, and to AWS with no rewriting. Amazon also said it’s going even further in its effort to loosen Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch. It is submitting code to the main PyTorch project that decouples various features from Nvidia’s chips, making it more open to any hardware by default.
Google may be one-upping Amazon in a few ways, however. It says it worked directly with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (maker of vLLM), RadixArk (maker of SGLang), and others to ensure that TorchTPU’s features and code libraries work well with these popular AI development tools, just as the original PyTorch does.
Plus the search giant has launched a dedicated tool, the TPU agent suite, to help developers move their apps to Google’s chips and cloud and fix errors along the way. It even updated its popular LiteRT tool, which runs AI on phones, laptops, and embedded devices, to work better with PyTorch AI apps.
None of this means AI app developers will automatically ditch Nvidia’s hardware en masse just because they can now easily move to alternative chips and clouds. But Amazon and Google are clearly working to end Nvidia’s advantage.

title_en: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
title_fa: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
excerpt_en: The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.
excerpt_fa: The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.
content_en:
OpenAI announced on Tuesday that users can now lock ChatGPT conversations to keep sensitive chats private when others may have access to their screen or device. Users can secure their locked chats with a four-digit PIN, or use Face ID or Touch ID on supported devices.
Unlike the app’s Temporary Chats, which provide a separate session that doesn’t appear in chat history, users can return to Locked Chats at any time.
The company says the feature is designed for situations where users might be discussing something personal or planning a surprise and want to keep those conversations private when handing their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.
The addition of locked chats adds a new layer of privacy to ChatGPT, as the app is increasingly used for personal conversations. Of course, while locking a chat can limit access, it doesn’t address concerns about how sensitive information is stored or handled.
OpenAI notes that locking a chat doesn’t create end-to-end encryption or a separate encrypted vault, change how long it retains the chat, remove information that ChatGPT remembered before a chat was locked, or change the “Improve the model for everyone” setting.
Once users lock a chat, it moves to a dedicated “Locked Chats” section, where it’s kept separate from regular chat history, pinned conversations, and chat search results.
With Memory enabled, Locked Chats has its own separate memory shared across conversations within the section. New messages sent after locking a chat can update that memory but don’t update regular Memory. That means new information from locked chats won’t leak into regular chats.
OpenAI says resetting a PIN permanently deletes all locked chats, files, and other content protected by the previous PIN.
Additionally, the Locked Chats option isn’t available for temporary chats, archived chats, group chats, chats created from a shared link, chats with scheduled tasks, and chats with meeting recordings.
Locked Chats will be available to users on ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans. The company notes that the feature is not available on ChatGPT for Healthcare. The feature is starting to roll out on Tuesday, so it may not be live yet for all users.

title_en: How long can you expect your original Steam Deck to last?
title_fa: How long can you expect your original Steam Deck to last?
excerpt_en: The original Steam Deck has been around for a while, but unless you only play the heaviest games, it should be great for some time more.
excerpt_fa: The original Steam Deck has been around for a while, but unless you only play the heaviest games, it should be great for some time more.
content_en:
How long can you expect your original Steam Deck to last?
The OG Steam Deck is starting to feel aged, but depending on your preferences, it can have a lot of life left.
Rumors of a Steam Deck 2 continue to buzz, even as RAMageddon has hit the current model and likely means its eventual successor will cost much more. Hype about a tech product's next-gen replacement tends to reflect, and instill, a sense that the current model is growing long in the tooth. If you have an original Steam Deck LCD, how much longer can you expect the device to last? That, of course, doesn't have a single answer.
The original Steam Deck offering something that felt fresh in 2022: a PC gaming handheld that could run everything from old favorites to many newer AAA releases. Four years later, the handheld PC market it spawned has grown considerably, with newer devices like the MSI Claw 8 EX pushing boundaries that the original Deck can't keep up with.
But that doesn't mean the OG Deck isn't still a terrific, well-balanced gaming portable. Despite its growing inability to handle the most demanding games, it's a device that, at least in theory, should keep you happy for some time. The biggest questions are parts longevity and how long you're willing to accept compromises.
Repair may beat replacement
Battery wear is one of the most likely reasons your Deck will eventually need some TLC. Although self-repair is possible, iFixit rates the procedure as difficult thanks to the battery being firmly glued in place. If you want to go the DIY route, watch multiple videos first to decide whether it's something you're comfortable with.
If you're less mechanically inclined, Valve's support team is the next step. Start a ticket to find out how much a repair will cost you, then weigh that against the cost of a new gaming handheld. Given how much the Steam Deck OLED and competitors have increased in price due to the RAM crisis, paying Valve to fix your original Steam Deck may be the better move.
A July 2026 scare had many Steam Deck LCD owners worrying their handheld was on its way out. A Reddit thread sparked this: someone shared a reply from iFixit support saying it had no immediate plans to restock OEM Steam Deck LCD batteries. An iFixit staffer confirmed in the comments that Valve was "just starting to sunset these parts." But Valve later said it would keep supplying batteries, and iFixit added that it would source aftermarket batteries if that ever changed. However, the price of the replacement batteries jumped from $80 to $130 when stock returned; iFixit currently offers an aftermarket battery for $80. Valve hasn't made long-term commitments for other parts, including the screen.
If other hardware fails, self-repair may be easier. In case you run into drift or other thumbstick problems, the sticks themselves are relatively easy to replace — no soldering required. iFixit sells replacements for $40 a pop. Once you're inside, other components can be swapped out with enough know-how: the Deck's SSD is removable with a single screw, and the fan pops out with a few more screws. Triggers, button input boards and the display take a bit more work, with the USB-C and microSD ports joining the battery as the hardest components to swap out.
If your Deck has a hardware failure, several options could be better than buying an expensive new handheld. Don't immediately write it off as the end of the line.
The software side is in better shape
Valve no longer sells the original Steam Deck LCD, but it still supports the device with software updates. In fact, that handheld runs the same software as the Steam Deck OLED, which the company still sells, so the OS front will likely be fine for the foreseeable future. Plus, the portable is now part of a larger ecosystem that includes the Steam Machine, new Steam Controller and Steam Frame, so Valve has extra incentive to keep its ecosystem running smoothly.
The Steam Deck's processor, GPU and 16GB of RAM likely put a lower ceiling on its longevity than Valve's support. Though the Steam Deck struggles with demanding modern games like Control Resonant, the platform is ubiquitous enough that many developers still go out of their way to optimize their games for the handheld. There's a wealth of supported games, and many developers will likely continue that practice for the foreseeable future — or at least until the Steam Deck 2 steals the spotlight.
That gives the original model some breathing room. And even as the list of unsupported new releases grows, there are still indie titles, retro games (emulated or native) and older AAA titles to give you plenty to play down the line. Plus then there's streaming from a PC, Steam Machine or cloud service. Unless your gaming tastes lean toward the latest GPU-intensive releases, you're likely to face battery or other hardware problems before you run out of fun titles.
So how long will your Deck stay useful? Roughly speaking: for indies, older games and emulation, years more. For new AAA releases, that window is already closing fast.

title_en: AMD is bringing its next-gen FSR 4.1 upscaling tech to Xbox
title_fa: AMD is bringing its next-gen FSR 4.1 upscaling tech to Xbox
excerpt_en: Coming soon to the X/S and Ally devices.
excerpt_fa: Coming soon to the X/S and Ally devices.
content_en:
AMD is bringing its next-gen FSR 4.1 upscaling tech to Xbox
It's coming soon to the X/S and Ally devices.
AMD just announced that it's bringing its FSR 4.1 upscaling tech to Xbox consoles. This includes the Xbox Series X/S and the Ally X, Ally X20, Ally S and Ally handheld consoles. FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) is a proprietary technology that renders a game at a lower resolution to conserve resources but uses machine learning to create a sharper image.
The Series X and Ally X are already very powerful, so the real benefit here will likely be for those who own the Series S, Ally S or the original Ally. These machines should experience a performance boost when FSR is activated.
"We've worked very closely with AMD to optimize this technology, giving developers another powerful tool for great performance and visual quality for players," said Xbox CTO Scott Van Vilet.
We don't have a timeline for this. There's a video that suggests FSR 4.1 will come to the Xbox Ally X before the end of the year, but the other consoles are listed as "coming soon" with no exact release window. Engadget has reached out to Microsoft to get a timeline and will update when we hear back.
AMD also announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to older RX 6000-series graphics cards and laptops powered by Ryzen AI 9 processors. The company has already made the tech available to 7000-series cards.
Sony has its own upscaling technology called Quick Spectral Super Resolution. This now supports some titles on the standard PS5 and works similarly to the pre-existing PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution upscaling software available on the PS5 Pro.

title_en: How often should you restart your Apple Watch?
title_fa: How often should you restart your Apple Watch?
excerpt_en: Your Apple Watch doesn't need frequent restarts like a computer, but you might still want to shut down when something's off.
excerpt_fa: Your Apple Watch doesn't need frequent restarts like a computer, but you might still want to shut down when something's off.
content_en:
How often should you restart your Apple Watch?
Your Apple Watch doesn't need constant maintenance, but reboots can help in some circumstances.
With most gadgets, it's an accepted rule that you should periodically restart them for the best performance. You might regularly restart your smartphone, and it's also relevant advice for everything from regularly rebooting your Wi-Fi router to gaming handhelds. In any event, a reboot doesn't usually hurt apart from the temporary downtime.
That downtime might matter in some cases though, particularly when it comes to wearables like the Apple Watch. Apart from not being able to easily check the time, you briefly lose conveniences like Apple Pay, walking directions or even digital car and house keys. Purists may resent the brief gap in their health and fitness data. When you're trying to close that Move ring, every minute counts.
Restarting your Apple Watch can occasionally be useful or critical. However, you probably don't need to make reboots a priority. Apple's design largely has this covered, since the company knows the product's limits and its role in your daily life.
Why you don't need to restart your Apple Watch often
Apple's watchOS is a complete operating system, running various apps and processes in much the same way as an iPhone or iPad. That means there are background processes and system caches, which are the key reasons why it's important to reboot other devices periodically. There's the potential for processes to become "stuck" or otherwise glitch out, in which case a restart will give them a fresh slate.
Meanwhile, if caches aren't periodically flushed, they can become so bloated that they eat into room needed for other functions. Apple specifically suggests restarting your Apple Watch if it doesn't have enough room for an update. You can also manually clear web-related content like cookies from your watch by going to Settings > General > Website Data > Clear Website Data.
All that said, watchOS is also lightweight by design. The apps that it runs (even real-time navigation tools like Apple Maps) are scaled back from their iPhone equivalents. You can't run nearly as much in the background as you might on a Mac or an iPad. Although there's no public-facing info about these caps, my Apple Watch Ultra 2 seemingly pushes the limit just by tracking a workout, listening to Apple Podcasts and following a Live Activity for Instacart. The device is quick to suspend apps beyond that kind of workload.
In practice, then, Apple seems to have built watchOS to keep its own house in order. This is borne out by hands-on use testing: with some Apple Watches, I've gone years without manually restarting them and there were no serious performance consequences. The reboots associated with installing new versions of watchOS appear to be enough to keep everything running smoothly.
When should you intentionally restart your Apple Watch?
Apple doesn't have any official guidance on this point. If you're noticing bugs, freezes or unexpected slowdowns, a restart should be your first troubleshooting step. You'll automatically clear your watch's cache and background processes, and there may not be much else you can do beyond installing any available software updates.
A restart is unavoidable if your Apple Watch becomes totally unresponsive. You can force a reboot by holding down the side button and Digital Crown simultaneously until the Apple logo appears. Whenever possible, Apple recommends the usual software-based shutdown instead: hold the side button until the slider menu appears, then tap the power icon and drag the Power Off slider. Once it's off, hold the side button again to power back on. You can't restart your watch while it's charging.
Our verdict is that when you're experiencing relatively smooth sailing, you don't need to worry about preventative Apple Watch reboots. Apple's software is engineered to run nonstop, no matter which watch model you own. For maintenance, you should be more concerned about app and OS updates, as well as keeping storage usage under control, so there's plenty of space for both updates and large caches.

With most gadgets, it's an accepted rule that you should periodically restart them for the best performance. You might regularly restart your smartphone, and it's also relevant advice for everything from regularly rebooting your Wi-Fi router to gaming handhelds. In any event, a reboot doesn't usually hurt apart from the temporary downtime.
That downtime might matter in some cases though, particularly when it comes to wearables like the Apple Watch. Apart from not being able to easily check the time, you briefly lose conveniences like Apple Pay, walking directions or even digital car and house keys. Purists may resent the brief gap in their health and fitness data. When you're trying to close that Move ring, every minute counts.
Restarting your Apple Watch can occasionally be useful or critical. However, you probably don't need to make reboots a priority. Apple's design largely has this covered, since the company knows the product's limits and its role in your daily life.
Why you don't need to restart your Apple Watch often
Apple's watchOS is a complete operating system, running various apps and processes in much the same way as an iPhone or iPad. That means there are background processes and system caches, which are the key reasons why it's important to reboot other devices periodically. There's the potential for processes to become "stuck" or otherwise glitch out, in which case a restart will give them a fresh slate.
Meanwhile, if caches aren't periodically flushed, they can become so bloated that they eat into room needed for other functions. Apple specifically suggests restarting your Apple Watch if it doesn't have enough room for an update. You can also manually clear web-related content like cookies from your watch by going to Settings > General > Website Data > Clear Website Data.
All that said, watchOS is also lightweight by design. The apps that it runs (even real-time navigation tools like Apple Maps) are scaled back from their iPhone equivalents. You can't run nearly as much in the background as you might on a Mac or an iPad. Although there's no public-facing info about these caps, my Apple Watch Ultra 2 seemingly pushes the limit just by tracking a workout, listening to Apple Podcasts and following a Live Activity for Instacart. The device is quick to suspend apps beyond that kind of workload.
In practice, then, Apple seems to have built watchOS to keep its own house in order. This is borne out by hands-on use testing: with some Apple Watches, I've gone years without manually restarting them and there were no serious performance consequences. The reboots associated with installing new versions of watchOS appear to be enough to keep everything running smoothly.
When should you intentionally restart your Apple Watch?
Apple doesn't have any official guidance on this point. If you're noticing bugs, freezes or unexpected slowdowns, a restart should be your first troubleshooting step. You'll automatically clear your watch's cache and background processes, and there may not be much else you can do beyond installing any available software updates.
A restart is unavoidable if your Apple Watch becomes totally unresponsive. You can force a reboot by holding down the side button and Digital Crown simultaneously until the Apple logo appears. Whenever possible, Apple recommends the usual software-based shutdown instead: hold the side button until the slider menu appears, then tap the power icon and drag the Power Off slider. Once it's off, hold the side button again to power back on. You can't restart your watch while it's charging.
Our verdict is that when you're experiencing relatively smooth sailing, you don't need to worry about preventative Apple Watch reboots. Apple's software is engineered to run nonstop, no matter which watch model you own. For maintenance, you should be more concerned about app and OS updates, as well as keeping storage usage under control, so there's plenty of space for both updates and large caches.

title_en: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei
title_fa: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei
excerpt_en: Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger.
excerpt_fa: Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger.
content_en:
Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger. The former Google CEO is reported to own about 1% of Anthropic after investing tens of millions of dollars in the leading AI lab’s Series A round in 2021, per Bloomberg. The startup was valued at $461 million at the time, according to PitchBook data.
If Bloomberg’s estimate is accurate, Schmidt’s stake is remarkably large compared with the 2% of the company that co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei holds. Anthropic is widely expected to go public before the end of the year, with top-end market estimates valuing the company at as much as $2 trillion. At that valuation, Schmidt would add as much as $20 billion to his net worth, which Bloomberg currently puts at $57.5 billion.
Schmidt has been an active tech investor since stepping down as Google CEO in 2011. He deploys capital through multiple entities, including Tomorrow Ventures, Innovation Endeavors Management, and his family office, Hillspire. His other AI bets include Mistral, General Intuition, and Reflection AI.
Schmidt and Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to our request for comment.

title_en: Meta’s Muse hits 10M US downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
title_fa: Meta’s Muse hits 10M US downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps
excerpt_en: New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.
excerpt_fa: New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.
content_en:
Meta’s AI companion, Muse, is now one of only a dozen mobile apps to have reached 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. According to new data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower, Muse has seen 10.9 million downloads since its September debut, 10.2 million of which were in the United States.
Only 11 other apps to date have reached this type of post-launch milestone, said Sensor Tower’s senior insights analyst Kara Lee. The most recent of these was Meta’s Threads, back in July 2023.
Other apps that saw this kind of scale were largely mobile games, Lee noted, like Fortnite, PUBG Mobile, Pokémon GO, and others. Besides Threads, Disney+ was the only other nongame app to make it into the exclusive club.
Meta’s success is tied to the company’s ability to scale its new apps by marketing them across its other services, which it has done with both Threads and Muse. Threads was built on top of Instagram’s social graph, and its content has been integrated into both Facebook and Instagram. However, Muse isn’t only benefiting from Meta’s ability to market the AI agent across its family of apps, which today includes 3.6 billion daily active users; the company is also heavily investing in advertising to drive new users to Muse.
Per Sensor Tower’s data, Meta has allocated 39% of its total advertising spend to market Muse in October, up from 23% last month. In addition, Muse now ranks as the 21st largest brand in the U.S. by advertising impressions this month, up from 73rd in September.
Still, marketing an app and retaining users after the initial shine wears off are two different things. In this case, Muse is seeing better retention rates than its AI competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok.
In the U.S., the app had a 30% retention rate after 7 days and a 23% retention rate after 14 days. By comparison, its rivals saw an average of a 19% 7-day retention rate and a 16% 14-day retention rate, according to the firm’s data.
Muse also hit another milestone that demonstrates active engagement with the AI app. Its daily active users reached 2.5 million for the first time on October 16, a 15% week-over-week increase.
Meta’s latest AI app, which can handle various tasks on users’ behalf, has seen breakout success since its debut. It shot up to No. 1 on the App Store and at one point even outpaced some of the metrics ChatGPT saw following its launch. Its latest milestone sees it topping its rivals again, as ChatGPT saw 3.7 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. Grok and Claude saw only 500,000 and 200,000 U.S. downloads, respectively, in their first 40 days.
Globally, ChatGPT beat out Muse, having scaled to around 15 million global downloads in its first 40 days. But this isn’t a fair comparison, as ChatGPT benefited from a wider reach. Muse is only available in the U.S. and Canada for now, while ChatGPT’s app attracted attention from markets like Japan, Brazil, and Germany, too. (Japan, for instance, accounted for 25% of its global installs during its first 40 days.)
Since launching, Muse has retained its No. 1 rank on the U.S. App Store for all days except October 19, when streaming app Kick briefly beat it out. It has since reclaimed the top spot as of Tuesday. Muse has also been No. 1 on Google Play over the past 30 days.
